value.rationale: Worst-case bounded edge-noise amplification of Hodge least-squares projection is a canonical stability question: the Hilbert orthogonal norm is always 1 but is uninformative for coordinatewise errors. The theorem gives an exact all-dimensional law with a nontrivial pairwise conductance decomposition, sharp and attained dimension-linear worst case (d+1)/2, a strict nonattained infimum 1 and explicit anisotropic tuning achieving every intermediate stability level. Nontrivial sign rigidity makes the sharp endpoint possible rather than a routine spectral norm bound.
